thesis: The bull establishes VT as an efficient strategic ownership vehicle through global breadth and 0.06% expenses, despite quantified US and technology concentration. That wins the allocation-utility argument but does not establish that increasing exposure now has a tactical return advantage. Neutral therefore preserves strategic ownership merit while withholding a timing call that the evidence cannot support.
strongest_counterexample: Broad index participation at very low cost does not need a breakout or near-term alpha to reward a disciplined long-horizon allocation; waiting for a tactical edge can sacrifice market participation.
invalidation_conditions: An issuer expense ratio above the current 0.06%, or a mandate change away from FTSE Global All Cap exposure, would invalidate the demonstrated low-cost global-allocation foundation.

A verified October premium/discount disclosure and an identified investor allocation shortfall would require reopening the timing/size ruling rather than inferring those facts from July portfolio valuation.
evidence_gaps: October 6 NAV premium/discount was not retrieved.
The research envelope does not establish the investor allocation shortfall or drawdown capacity needed to size an increase.
decisive_factors: June weights of 61.9% US, 33.3% technology and 21.7% top ten retain correlated drawdown risk while preserving genuine breadth.
July 20.8x portfolio P/E is not October fair value; corporate debt and FCF measures do not apply.
